review: Official visitor material confirms the controlled one-way itinerary and endpoints but does not publish an orthographic plan of the corridor body. The official access PDF maps only the route through the Uffizi to D19; those Uffizi floors are owned by the main task and do not establish corridor geometry. Two independently published aerials were explicitly tested as rectification candidates rather than rejected merely for being oblique. Both are perspective images of non-coplanar ground, roofs, facades and elevated corridor segments, with height-dependent parallax and roof occlusion; neither one affine inverse nor one planar homography can recover the corridor interior. The 2025 Uffizi CIG B78AF05213 notice confirms that a procurement package for climate works in a corridor portion exists and directs bidders to the official procurement portal. The downloadable official notice contains no plan, while the procurement portal returned HTTP 403 in both a direct request and a visible browser. A third-party index names an attachment category 'Planimetria' but exposes no authoritative attachment URL, so it is retained only as a discovery lead. No legacy corridor line was retained.

rectificationReview.candidate: single affine or planar projective rectification to a top view
observations: The photograph visibly includes vertical facades as well as roofs and ground, proving that the mapped evidence is distributed across different depth and height planes rather than one parallel projection plane.
Long architectural axes undergo perspective foreshortening and convergence; an affine inverse cannot restore parallel top-view geometry.

A homography could rectify one selected plane only. The corridor changes elevation and runs across roofs, bridge fabric and building interiors, so a ground-plane homography would displace its elevated segments by height-dependent parallax.

Roofs and adjoining buildings occlude the corridor's interior walls, doors, width changes and junctions. The source provides no measured control points or surveyed corridor outline with which to reconstruct the hidden boundaries.
rectificationReview.conclusion: The aerial supports city-scale route context only. It cannot be converted into an evidence-backed indoor top-view model without inventing concealed geometry.

sources.title: Vasari Corridor reopening works tender
sources.finding: The official tender record was investigated as the likeliest route to project drawings. No retrievable public technical plan of the complete corridor body was available during this review, so no geometry was derived from search-result descriptions.

sources.title: Vasari Corridor works tender archive
sources.finding: Investigated as a possible route to technical plans; no publicly linked orthographic corridor-body plan suitable for extraction was identified.

sources.title: Avviso preventivo di procedura negoziata · CIG B78AF05213
sources.finding: The two-page official notice concerns completion of climate and humidity-control systems in a portion of the Vasari Corridor and directs the procedure to https://portalegare.uffizi.it/. It contains no plan, dimensions or attachment links.

sources.title: Portale Gare Telematiche
sources.finding: Investigated by direct HTTP request and visible browser on 2026-09-05; both returned HTTP 403 Forbidden before any public tender search or attachment list could be reached. No credentials or restricted access were attempted.

sources.title: Dettaglio CIG B78AF05213
sources.finding: The public detail route and its API were investigated. The API response required anti-spam tokens and did not expose technical attachments; no plan URL was recovered.

sources.title: Manifestazione di Interesse · CIG B78AF05213
sources.finding: The third-party index lists an attachment category named 'Planimetria', but it provides no authoritative downloadable plan URL. This is not treated as evidence for geometry.

sources.authority: Societa Italiana per il Restauro dell'Architettura
sources.title: Fragile da conservare. Percorsi di conoscenza per i restauri del Corridoio Vasariano agli Uffizi
sources.finding: The article's figure 3 is a perspective aerial overview and the remaining inspected figures are historical or interior photographs. No orthographic corridor plan is published. The aerial has the same non-coplanar parallax and occlusion limits recorded in rectificationReview.
